# IEditSurface&lt;TPixel&gt;

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Editing` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public interface IEditSurface<TPixel> where TPixel : struct
```

A fixed-size, randomly-addressable raster the edit commands paint on, generic over the pixel it stores: [`ValueMap`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ValueMap.md) supplies [`GrayPixel`](Nfty.Core.Editing.GrayPixel.md), [`ColorMap`](Nfty.Core.Editing.ColorMap.md) supplies `Rgba32`. The commands hold geometry only — every "what does this pixel become" decision travels as a `TPixel`, so one implementation of disc stamping, shape rasterising, region scanning and the undo snapshot serves both surfaces.

**Type parameters**

- `TPixel` - The pixel this surface stores.

## Remarks

[`IEditSurface<TPixel>.AlphaOf()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.IEditSurface-1.md#m-alphaof-0) and [`IEditSurface<TPixel>.WithAlpha()`](Nfty.Core.Editing.IEditSurface-1.md#m-withalpha-0-system-byte) are here rather than on the pixel because `Rgba32` is ImageSharp's type and cannot be made to implement an interface of ours. They carry format knowledge only — where this surface's pixel keeps its alpha — never policy: the opacity lock's rule lives once in [`RegionEditCommand<TPixel>`](Nfty.Core.Editing.RegionEditCommand-1.md), so the two surfaces have nothing to keep in step and nothing to drift apart on.
